findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how eval runs treat the production fallback chain: either DISABLE fallback for eval runs (Bedrock-only, fail loudly on a Bedrock error and abort/resume the run) or make the per-review model-parity guard operate PER RESULT (reject/quarantine any review whose recorded provider_provenance.ran_model is not the expected Bedrock id), so a mid-run failover cannot silently produce a heterogeneous, partially-uncached run.
evidence: Invariant 2 constrains only START/CONFIG time: the harness 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' and 'refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ' — nothing governs an in-run failover.

The production runner drives a FallbackModel chain: `should_fall_back` (src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:366) returns True for the availability classes AND `ResolutionClass.CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL`, i.e. it will move to the next configured candidate, which may be a NON-Bedrock provider (the mixed Bedrock+Anthropic chain the invariant itself warns 'silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost').

The fallen-over model is what gets recorded: `provider_provenance['ran_model'] = ran_model` is set to the model that actually answered (src/rebar/llm/runner.py:712-713), so a mid-run failover yields per-review results whose ran_model legitimately differs from the Bedrock primary — inside one run, which the plan assumes is homogeneous.

The Tier-1 seam is the real verifier: `verify_findings(..., run_chunk=…)` (src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:345) drives the production LLM path, so eval re-runs inherit the fallback chain unless the plan disables it.
findings.finding: Invariant 2 (model parity / homogeneous Bedrock chain) does not specify the eval run's behavior when a Bedrock LLM call FAILS MID-RUN and the production FallbackModel chain would fail over to a configured fallback target on a different provider/model — an unspecified fallback for a failed sub-step on the LLM surface the eval re-runs through.
findings.location: Approach → Invariant 2 (Model parity); Tier-1 and Tier-2 runners
scenarios: A Tier-1 reproduction run (the one that establishes the verifier noise floor) hits a transient Bedrock 5xx/throttle on review #400 of a batch; the chain fails over to Anthropic for that review only. Prompt caching silently disables for those calls (cost/measurement confound), and that review's ran_model is anthropic:… — so the run is no longer homogeneous, yet nothing refuses it because the START-time guard already passed.

The commissioning Tier-2 Opus baseline run partially fails over; the ledger/report shows a mix of Bedrock and non-Bedrock ran_model ids, contradicting AC7's 'ledger showing only Bedrock Opus/Sonnet ids'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Invariant 2: 'Eval runs configure NO fallback chain for the frontier/standard class (or set should_fall_back to reject every failover); a Bedrock call failure aborts the affected review and is retried on Bedrock, never relocated. Independently, every persisted eval result is validated PER REVIEW against the expected Bedrock per-pass model id via provider_provenance.ran_model, and any result whose ran_model differs is dropped from the run and flagged, not diffed.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Tier-1/Tier-2 with ADR 0054 §2 (which rejects purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review sweeps as calibration instruments): explicitly invoke §2's prompt-development/regression-pinning carve-out, and state which tier is permitted for which change class (esp. that Pass-3 threshold/formula changes are calibration and must be justified by Tier-0 replay, not Tier-1/Tier-2).
evidence: Plan: 'Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay (Sonnet …). Re-run the verifier … Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay (Opus …). Re-run finders … on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)'
Plan invariant 3 cites ADR 0054 only for offline-Tier-0 support: 'Consistent with ADR 0054 (the field corpus is the instrument)'

docs/adr/0054-...md §2: 'The following MUST NOT be required, planned, or commissioned … Purpose-built LLM eval suites … Bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan / review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored.'
docs/adr/0054 §2 carve-out (uncited by the plan): 'It says nothing about evals used for their own purposes (prompt development, regression pinning of model behavior, capability checks).'
findings.finding: The plan cites ADR 0054 only as support for its offline-first invariant, but ADR 0054 §2 explicitly REJECTS 'purpose-built LLM eval suites' and 'bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan/review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored' as calibration instruments; the plan's Tier-1 and Tier-2 are exactly those, and the Pass-3 threshold/formula assessment case is squarely calibration (ADR 0054's domain). The plan does not confront this tension or invoke ADR 0054 §2's carve-out for prompt-development/regression-pinning evals.
findings.location: Approach → Tier 1 / Tier 2; Non-negotiable invariant 3 ('Consistent with ADR 0054 … and with 6982's rejection of live A/B')
scenarios: A reviewer or operator asks why this epic commissions the very LLM re-review sweeps ADR 0054 §2 names as rejected; the plan's own citation of ADR 0054 as support makes the contradiction sharper.
A Pass-3 threshold change assessed via Tier-1/Tier-2 (rather than Tier-0 alone) — that is calibration, where ADR 0054's rejection is fully in force.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'ADR 0054 reconciliation' paragraph: Tier-0 is the ADR-0054-mandated corpus replay; Tier-1/Tier-2 are scoped strictly to Pass-2/Pass-1 PROMPT-and-question REGRESSION detection (§2's 'prompt development / regression pinning of model behavior' carve-out), never as the instrument for a threshold/formula calibration, which ADR 0054 restricts to Tier-0 replay + dogfooding.

evidence: ADR 0054 §2: 'The following MUST NOT be required, planned, or commissioned … Purpose-built LLM eval suites built for a single calibration question. Bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan / review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored.'
The plan invokes ADR 0054 as SUPPORT ('Consistent with ADR 0054') but only for Tier 0; Tier 1/2 are bulk LLM re-runs.

ADR 0054 §2 last paragraph DOES carve out 'evals used for their own purposes (prompt development, regression pinning of model behavior, capability checks)' and the existing ab_impact_model.py — a reconciliation path the plan does not invoke.
findings.finding: The plan's Tier-1 (re-run the verifier over the corpus) and Tier-2 (re-run finders over a sample) are precisely the 'purpose-built LLM eval suite' and 'bulk re-review sweep' categories that ADR 0054 §2 explicitly REJECTS, yet the plan cites ADR 0054 only as support for its offline-first/Tier-0 stance and never reconciles the LLM tiers against that rejection.
findings.location: Approach — 'Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay', 'Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay'; Invariant 3 'Offline first … Consistent with ADR 0054'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph (and a line in the ADR this epic ships) explicitly citing ADR 0054 §2's carve-out for 'regression pinning of model behavior / capability checks', framing Tier-1/2 as building a standing instrument (not gating a single calibration value), and bounding when a Tier-1/2 run is permitted vs when Tier-0 alone suffices.

evidence: Approach Tier 2: 'Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached, plus a Tier-1 run on the new findings'.

Approach invariant 2 rationale: 'the mixed Bedrock+Anthropic fallback silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost' — the plan treats caching as the cost lever, but the environment (bedrock-access.md, test_bedrock_provider.py) shows Opus-on-Bedrock never caches regardless of provider homogeneity.
T3 evidence class for the Opus caching assumption underlying the budget: CONTRADICTED for Opus, so an uncached Tier-2 estimate is the only sound basis.
findings.finding: The Tier-2 cost figure ('~$3.4/review uncached') and the $120 commissioning / $200-cap budget do not state whether the budget assumes prompt caching for Opus. Given Opus is measured NOT to cache on Bedrock (invariant 2's mandated Pass-1 path), the Tier-2 budget MUST be computed uncached; the plan should make that assumption explicit so the pre-flight cost estimate and the hard-cap guard are grounded in the real (non-caching) Opus billing rather than an unverified caching assumption.
findings.location: Approach, Tier 2 bullet ('Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached'); invariant 1 (hard budget, $120 commissioning / $200 cap)
scenarios: The pre-flight cost estimator applies a caching discount to Opus Tier-2 calls; actual Bedrock billing charges full input every call; projected spend understates real spend and the $200 hard cap is breached mid-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Annotate the Tier-2 cost bullet and invariant 1 to record 'Opus/Tier-2 priced uncached — Bedrock Opus caching is measured ineffective (ADR 0059 §7)'; reserve the caching discount for Tier-1/Sonnet only in the estimator.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the plan_replay novelty vs the existing src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py prompt-eval framework (reuse vs new package, and why) and rebut 6982's 're-running the gate's own verifier is circular' lesson for Tier-2 (e.g. reliance on the outcome labels / noise-floor as construct-valid ground truth rather than self-adjudication).
evidence: Plan proposes 'New package src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/' without mentioning the sibling src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py.

src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py docstring: 'Prompt evaluation — regression detection + CI gating for git-canonical prompts … a git-tracked eval spec beside each prompt … dataset, thresholds, scorers … result gates CI.'

Ticket 6982 comment (candidate ADR): 'an adjudicator must be at least as capable … as the gate it judges, and re-running the gate's own verifier is circular — prefer CONSTRUCT-VALID ground truth … over LLM-adjudicated finding labels.'

Web prior art (retrieved): offline-first LLM eval/replay harnesses for 'did this prompt/model change make things better or worse?' with golden sets and CI regression gates are a well-trodden, off-the-shelf pattern (e.g. multiple public 'llm-eval-harness' projects).
findings.finding: The plan does not justify the novelty of an LLM-re-run harness (Tier-1/Tier-2) against two adjacent prior instruments it should confront: (a) the shipped in-repo prompt-eval framework src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py (git-canonical .rebar/evals/*.eval.yaml specs, golden datasets, deterministic-scorer gates, pinned-grader discipline, CI gating) — a 'did this prompt change make things better/worse' harness of exactly this shape — and (b) 6982's recorded methodological lesson that 're-running the gate's own verifier is circular'. This is an anti-repackaging / Rule-of-Three gap.
findings.location: Scope ('New package src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/'); Approach → Tier 1 / Tier 2
scenarios: A new evals/plan_replay/ tier-runner duplicates dataset/scorer/gate machinery that eval.py already provides for git-canonical prompts.

Tier-2 scores a candidate finder against finding sets produced by the same finder/verifier family, reproducing the circularity 6982 flagged, without the construct-valid ground truth that lesson recommends.

scenarios: A described deliverable ships (or silently does not) with no test/manifest gating its completion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the stratification dimensions and selection rule for the ~20-ticket Tier-2 sample (and how it is frozen in the corpus manifest).
evidence: Approach: "Re-run finders with candidate criteria on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)".
AC 5: "...on a fixed stratified sample..." — the strata (by criterion? verdict? outcome label? store?) are never named.
Signal (1)/(2): sample-selection protocol is a data-design decision left implicit.
findings.finding: The stratified sample (~20 tickets) has no stated stratification dimensions, so the frozen sample is not reproducibly definable.
findings.location: Approach, Tier 2 ("a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets)") and AC 5
scenarios: Two executors build differently composed 20-ticket samples; Tier-2 results are not comparable across proposals despite the sample being called 'fixed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify strata (e.g. stratify by triggered criterion and by verdict class, seeded deterministically, recorded in the manifest).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the noise band is computed from the 208 identical-material flips + Tier-1 reproduction, and the exact comparison that classifies a delta as improve / regress / indistinguishable.
evidence: Invariant 4: "reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run".
No stated aggregation: is the band a raw count, a proportion, a confidence interval, a multiple of the flip rate? Signal (2): a derived metric with no computation protocol.
findings.finding: The noise-aware acceptance rule references a 'noise band' but does not state how the band is computed into an accept/regress/improve threshold.
findings.location: Approach, invariant 4 ("Noise-aware acceptance") and AC 4/AC 8
scenarios: Two analysts compute the band differently (e.g. std-dev vs percentile) and reach opposite improve/regress verdicts on the same delta.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the band as e.g. a confidence interval on the identical-material flip rate combined with per-question reproduction variance, and state the delta-vs-band comparison rule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'friction rate' (its numerator/denominator and the corpus signal it derives from) in the plan.
evidence: AC 3 lists "friction rate" among diff-report metrics.
Absence: 'friction' is never defined; there is no formula relating it to verdict flips, revise→re-review pairs, or block_threshold. Signal (2): derived metric with no computation.
findings.finding: AC 3 requires reporting a 'friction rate' but no computation or aggregation protocol for it is given anywhere in the plan.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, item 3 ("...label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate...")
scenarios: Implementer invents a friction-rate definition; a later reviewer disputes it and the Tier-0 report is re-derived.
findings.suggested_fix: State e.g. friction rate = fraction of reviews that would flip PASS→BLOCK (extra revise cycles) under the candidate overlay, computed over the corpus.

findings.finding: Child 98df performs LIVE LLM eval calls ('rebar criteria eval project.measurement-provenance --runs 3') but is not routed through the epic's mandatory budget ledger, $200 cap, or Bedrock-only model-parity guard, contradicting the parent's non-negotiable invariant that EVERY eval call is priced/ledgered and pinned to Bedrock. 98df is not listed among the parent's folded-in work either, so its live spend is owned by no budget-tracking child.
findings.location: child 98df-3528-9b1f-405a
scenarios: 98df's --runs 3 live eval executes outside the ledger, so its dollars are invisible to the $200 cap accounting and its model provider is not guaranteed Bedrock, confounding the epic's parity invariant and its cost-close accounting.
